item.title: Divine Word University introduces laptops, upgrades technology for 2026
item.description: Divine Word University (DWU) is introducing new technology and learning systems for 2026 to improve student access and teaching quality. Every student will receive a laptop as part of the university’s paperless learning system. The laptops come with a three-year warranty, ensuring students are supported throughout their studies. Fr. item.title: Simbu’s Shalom Sam Bire signs with Nowra-Bomaderry Jets
item.description: Shalom Sam Bire, a talented rugby league player from Simbu Province has signed with the Nowra-Bomaderry Jets for the 2026 Group 7 Rugby League season in Australia. item.description: Hundreds of students in Madang cannot progress to grade nine, grade eleven, or tertiary institutions due to delays in issuing certificates. item.title: Free tickets to BTS’s comeback performance to open on Feb. 23
item.description: Mark Feb. 23 on your calendars: online reservations for BTS's comeback live performance in Seoul will open to the public for free. The "Arirang" live performance is scheduled for March 21 at 8 p.m. in central Seoul's Gwanghwamun Square. Booking will open at 8 p.m. on Feb. 23 via NOL Ticket. Reservations are free for everyone, and detailed instructions will be uploaded to the ticketing website on Feb. 20. item.title: Bougainville generates K750m in Cocoa revenue, assumes full control of export system
item.description: The Autonomous Bougainville Government (ABG) has announced a record-breaking cocoa production year for 2025, generating an estimated K750 million in revenue, with approximately K600 million flowing directly to farmers. This milestone coincides with Bougainville taking full administrative control of its cocoa export industry for the first time. item.title: Polytech academic staff stage two-weeks sit-in protest
item.description: The academic staff of the National Polytechnic Institute have begun their two-weeks sit in protest today, following delays by DHERST to favorably respond to their petition. Their petition was presented to DHERST last July, to which the secretary responded with commitments to address the issues raised; however, not much has been done since then.
